hero.title: How it was built
hero.subtitle: Software engineering without compromises
hero.lead: The internal anatomy of this portfolio: four audiences, four frameworks, solo developer and zero backend, with strict performance budgets and explicit contracts.

architecture.title: Composition without Module Federation
architecture.lead: Rather than relying on heavy runtime orchestration libraries, each microfrontend is compiled independently and wrapped in a Custom Element (Web Component). A vanilla JavaScript shell orchestrates on-demand loading based on the URL route.

apps.name: Vanilla Shell
apps.description: Root document, header, footer, and dynamic microfrontend mounting. Under 2 kB of JS.

boundaries: No MFE imports code from another MFE or application.
Cross-area communication happens exclusively through typed events (@portfolio/contracts).
Centralized data validated with Zod in @portfolio/content; no app embeds custom JSON.
Colors, spacing, and typography consumed strictly via semantic tokens (@portfolio/tokens).
Reusable UI components reside in the Lit design system (@portfolio/design-system).
Each MFE is loaded only on its own route and runs independently in development.
architecture.pipelineDescription: Each package compiles its own artifacts incrementally using Turborepo (pnpm build). The pnpm assemble script gathers all packages into the dist/ directory, producing a 100% static site with Content-Security-Policy and SHA-256 hashes computed at build time.

adrs.title: 16 Architecture Decisions (ADRs)
adrs.lead: Every architectural choice was documented and version-controlled in docs/architecture/adr/. No decision is made silently.

adrs.summary: Microfrontends with five technologies: Next.js on home and static pages, Vue for recruiter, Angular for technical, React for client, and vanilla Shell.
Browser composition via Custom Elements: native isolation through Web Components without the overhead or fragility of Module Federation or single-spa.
Universal Web Component design system using Lit and CSS tokens, ensuring uniform consumption across any framework without heavy wrappers.
Initial hosting and deployment (superseded by ADR 0007 for automated GitHub Actions and Vercel deployments).
Semantic theme control in the design system via data-theme on <html>, preventing theme flash with localStorage persistence.
Language switching via HTML document links: each language has its own canonical URL, with zero runtime global state owners.
Static hosting and deployment on Vercel via GitHub Actions with full CI gate checks prior to release.
Route behavior belongs to the route's owner app: no shared library injects logic into another microfrontend's route.
Isolated internal page stages in dedicated CSS, preventing global style leaks across distinct microfrontends.
Content stage and entry transitions connecting the immersive home page to the themed areas.
Bidirectional transitions between home and target areas with sessionStorage flags and pure CSS themed curtains.
Site x-ray in a versioned data file (site.json), generated from real build measurements and Lighthouse CI audits.
Content pages on Next.js routes as Server Components with isolated styles in public/, without inflating the route JS bundle.
Protected branches (development and production), two isolated environments, and automated semantic releases.
Language-scoped content bundles in microfrontends: each MFE compiles dedicated entry points to fetch only the active language JSON.

Themed mascot AI assistant powered by Google Gemini via Vercel Serverless Function (/api/chat) and Lit Web Component in the design system, enforcing connect-src 'self' CSP and zero credential exposure.

designSystem.title: Universal Web Components & CSS Tokens
designSystem.lead: A single Lit component library serves every framework, ensuring strict visual fidelity without proprietary framework wrappers.

points.title: Lit & Custom Elements
points.text: Native browser components encapsulated with Shadow DOM. The design system bundle is loaded only once by the shell or Next.js layout.

points.title: Semantic CSS Tokens
points.text: Colors, typography, spacing, and border radii defined in CSS custom properties. Zero JavaScript runtime overhead for theme switching.

points.title: Universal Accessibility
points.text: Keyboard navigation, visible focus indicators, WCAG AA contrast in both themes, and screen reader announcements built into every component.

metrics.title: Real Metrics & Performance Budgets
metrics.lead: Measured and verified data in the CI/CD pipeline via Lighthouse CI and strict bundle budget checkers. Zero network waterfalls.
metrics.zeroWaterfallText: Every route ships its content pre-bundled for the current language. Custom elements render immediately with no subsequent API roundtrips.
